turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Morning. Have a seat there. What can I do for you?

[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): It's the burning when I go to the toilet, doctor. Back again. I was supposed to be at the hairdresser's at half twelve and I very nearly stayed on the bus, only I couldn't face another day of it. The Ennis bus was late anyhow, some tractor on the road.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): How long has the burning been there?
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Since Sunday. Well, actually it started Saturday night, after the hurling in the park. So that's three days... hang on, today's Wednesday, Saturday to now is four days.
[SEG0005] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any blood in the urine?
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): No blood. I kept looking, like an eejit, and there wasn't any.
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): Going more often than usual?

[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): Ah I am. Every half hour, near enough. And I have to go the second I feel it or I won't make it. I work in the credit union, and the customers can hear the door of the loo, it's mortifying.
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): Pain in the back or the side?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): No, the back is grand. There's a wee ache low down at the front, a pressure more than a pain.
[SEG0011] person_1 (DOCTOR): Fever? Shivering?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): No fever. I stuck the thermometer in this morning before I left the house and it was normal. No shivers.
[SEG0013] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any vaginal discharge, or itching?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No, nothing like that. Sure I'm scarlet even saying the words.
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): Is this the first time this year?

[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): Third time this year. Wait now, I'm wrong. There was the one in February as well, after my sister's wedding, so maybe the fourth. The hat she had on would take your eye out, feathers and all, but that's not why I'm here.
[SEG0017] person_1 (DOCTOR): What have you taken for it?

[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): My sister had leftover antibiotic in the press. I thought it was amoxicillin. No, it was trimethoprim, she said, the little white ones. I took two days of them, and I know I shouldn't have touched another person's tablets.
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): What dose did you take?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): Two hundred milligrams... no, sorry, they were the hundred milligram ones. One in the morning and one at night. I stopped yesterday when the strip ran out.
[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): Were you on a regular prevention antibiotic before that?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes. A nightly trimethoprim after the January bout, and I stopped it in March. My stomach couldn't stick it.
[SEG0023] person_1 (DOCTOR): Strength?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): A hundred milligrams, at night.
[SEG0025] person_1 (DOCTOR): Did you take the pivmecillinam from the last visit?
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): I never took that. I never even collected it from the chemist. It felt like a fuss over nothing at the time, which is gas now.
[SEG0027] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any medicines you are actually on?
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): The pill, Microlite, one every day. That's it, apart from those tablets I borrowed.
[SEG0029] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any drug allergies?
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): No. None at all.
[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'll ask once more. Any discharge or itch, even a small bit?
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): Ah, God. Alright. There's a small bit of white discharge the last two days, and it is itchy, not heavy. I was hoping you'd not ask twice.
[SEG0033] person_1 (DOCTOR): Does the urine smell?
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): Strong, yes. Same as the last time. I've been on the tea all day thinking I'd flush it out. My mother swore by barley water but I can't stand the smell of that either.
[SEG0035] person_1 (DOCTOR): Nausea or vomiting?
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Stomach's been fine since I came off the nightly tablet.
[SEG0037] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any chance you're pregnant?
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): No chance. No fella since Christmas, and I'm strict with the pill. I was going to tell you about the wedding playlist, they had the worst band.

[SEG0039] person_1 (DOCTOR): Leave the band. My impression is another cystitis, provisional until the lab looks at it, given four days of burning and frequency with no fever and no back pain. I'm not calling this a kidney infection. The itch might be thrush from the trimethoprim you borrowed; I can't rule that out, and I won't decide that today.
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): Thrush? I knew I shouldn't have taken her yoke. Is the kidney thing off the table? I had myself buried after a thing I read on the bus.
[SEG0041] person_1 (DOCTOR): Off the table from what you've said. I'll send a urine sample to the lab today.
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): And a tablet of my own, I hope, not hers.
[SEG0043] person_1 (DOCTOR): Nitrofurantoin, by mouth, a hundred milligrams twice a day for three days. Take it with food.
[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): Do I stop the pill while I'm on that?
[SEG0045] person_1 (DOCTOR): No. Stay on the pill. Drink more water, and don't borrow antibiotics again.
[SEG0046] person_1 (DOCTOR): If this hasn't settled in a week, come back. We might do a kidney scan if it does not settle.
[SEG0047] person_2 (PATIENT): A scan, Lord. Right so. I'll do the sample on the way out. Thanks, doctor.

spec.situation: Woman with burning urine again; says 'third time this year' then corrects to 'maybe the fourth'; took leftover antibiotic from a sister; embarrassed; vaginal symptoms denied, then partly admitted. Urine test ordered.
features: stopped_or_never_taken: a medicine the patient stopped, was never given or only took once ('I stopped it in March'). Status discontinued, not current; a medicine never taken is not recorded as a medication.
hedged_plan: the doctor hedges ('we might do a scan if it does not settle', 'let's see in two weeks'). Conditional vs planned status must follow the words.

doctor_thinks_aloud: the doctor lists possible causes or says what they will not conclude yet. Only record a clinical assessment if the doctor actually states a leading or differential impression; 'let's see what the tests say' is not an assessment.
self_correction: a speaker states a number, drug name or duration and then corrects it in the same turn or later ('seventy-five... no, hundred and fifty'). The label holds only the corrected value.

omissions.text: Negative finding initially recorded as no vaginal discharge or itching was later corrected by the patient: there has been a small amount of white discharge for the last 2 days and it is itchy, not heavy.
The patient said she never took/never collected the previously prescribed pivmecillinam from the chemist.
Instruction for the planned nitrofurantoin was to take it with food.
Doctor specifically stated they were not calling this a kidney infection / kidney involvement was off the table based on the history given.
